Process improvement.

Find where work waits, fails or gets repeated, then test changes with the people doing the work.

Discuss this service View brief

Scope of work.

Map one process

Interview staff and trace a real job from request to completion. Handoffs, rework and waiting time are marked on a shared map.

Pilot a specific fix

Rank bottlenecks by evidence and effort. Introduce a simple procedure or checklist, with a named owner and a date to review the change.

Compare and hand over

Measure the same cycle time or error rate before and after the pilot. Document the revised process and train those who will use it.

What you receive.

  • A map of a real workflow, including delay and rework.
  • A tested change, written procedure and handover to staff.
  • A review of agreed measures after 30 and 90 days.

Common questions.

How long is a single workflow project?

Four to eight weeks is typical. Larger programmes can be divided into separately reviewed phases.

Which measures suit a pilot?

Choose two or three before making a change. Turnaround time, repeat errors and staff hours are examples that can be checked again afterwards.

Can we use the software we already have?

Yes. The team starts with existing tools and considers an additional system only where the expected benefit justifies it.
